conclusion: Existing 971 legacy cards reviewed individually in v184, but not all AQA spec requirements nor original full question archive. Rather than duplicate the known formulae and definitions, add 13 context-dependent single-answer cards and eight original combined analytical questions with theoretical observations and calculations.

newCards.front: For an aldehyde, what positive observation is expected with Fehling's solution?
A known carbonyl compound is either an aldehyde or a ketone. Fehling's solution remains blue. Which is more likely?
Which gas accounts for effervescence when a carboxylic acid reacts with a carbonate?
In acid-catalysed hydrolysis of an ester, is the acid-derived organic product a carboxylic acid or its salt?
In alkaline hydrolysis of an ester, what form of the acid-derived product is formed before any acidification?
What three-carbon alcohol is produced when a triglyceride undergoes hydrolysis?
What class of organic product forms when an acyl chloride reacts with a primary amine?
If the net exponent on partial pressure in a Kp expression is +1, what are its units when pressures are in kPa?
If the net exponent on partial pressure in a Kp expression is −1, what are its units when pressures are in kPa?
At a fixed temperature, what happens to pH when [H⁺] increases by a factor of ten?
If [H⁺] doubles, by approximately how many units does pH fall?
An organic mass spectrum shows an M and M+2 molecular-ion pair in about a 3:1 intensity ratio. Which halogen atom is indicated?
The molecular ion of Br₂ gives three isotope peaks at m/z 158, 160 and 162. What is their approximate relative intensity ratio?

limitations: Original model answers are not an AQA official mark scheme and unfamiliar valid workings may require manual review.
Historical past papers 2015–2026 have not been exhaustively question-indexed.
AQA Chemistry 3.1.12 in full includes content not taught for the school mock; cards here remain inside pH/Kw/weak acids only.
